body:
Each line break in documentation creates a new paragraph, so try to use line breaks more sparingly to avoid creating too many paragraphs:

```suggestion
				Creates the BVH tree from an array of faces. Each 3 vertices of the input [param faces] array represent one triangle (face).
				Returns [code]true[/code] if the tree is successfully built, [code]false[/code] otherwise.
```

Also, writing numbers with digits is preferred as it makes them stand out more.

body:
Mention a concrete example use case:

```suggestion
		Creates a bounding volume hierarchy (BVH) tree structure around triangle geometry. The triangle BVH tree can be used for efficient intersection queries without involving a physics engine. For example, this can be used in editor tools to select objects with complex shapes based on the mouse cursor position.
		[b]Performance:[/b] Creating the BVH tree for complex geometry is a slow process and best done in a background thread.
```
Is there a convention for script wrapper methods? I like this new descriptive style.

I dont think `_xyz` underscore function names should be used for this as it creates naming conflicts quickly with functions that are used for actual virtual call overrides as they all follow the underscore convention and are exposed with those names to users and documentation.

You can see the created travesty all over the Godot code base when a class has to bind its `xyz_function()` to `_xyz_function()` for scripting and its actual `_xyz_function()` virtual to `_xyz_virtual_call_function()` because the name is already taken. That creates a confusing mess for no reason.
